### Joyful Generosity
Author: Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/article/joyful-generosity
Passage: 2 Corinthians 9:7
Points:
- Scripture emphasizes that God loves a genuinely cheerful and joyful giver.
- Believers honor God by actively stepping out in bold generosity rather than holding back out of fear.
- We must examine our motivations so giving springs from care rather than guilt or compulsion.
- Remembering God's promises assures us that bountiful sowers will experience a bountiful harvest.
- Reflecting on God’s kindness naturally inspires a glad and openhearted response.

### God Is Looking at Your Heart
Author: Rick Warren
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-hope-with-rick-warren/daily-hope-with-rick-warren-september-3-2026.html
Passage: 2 Corinthians 9:7
Points:
- God values a willing and sincere heart far more than mere financial capacity.
- Genuine giving is thoughtful, intentional, and planned rather than done impulsively.
- Offerings should never be forced by external pressure but given voluntarily from the heart.
- God delights when His people give with enthusiasm and joyful cheerfulness.

### The Grace of Cheerful Giving
Author: Frank Cavalli
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/grace-cheerful-giving
Passage: 2 Corinthians 9:6-8
Points:
- Fear of loss often holds people back, but Scripture compares giving to agricultural sowing.
- How believers give matters to God just as much as what they give.
- God desires voluntary offerings marked by ease, pleasure, and freedom from grief.
- Joyful giving during hardship provides a distinct witness to the grace of Christ.
- Sacrificial generosity is not natural human behavior but an empowering work of the Spirit.

### The Marks of a Giver
Author: Michael Youssef
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-week-of-october-25.html
Passage: 2 Corinthians 9:7
Points:
- Money is intended to serve God’s kingdom rather than become our master.
- Tangible giving demonstrates that God owns every resource, not merely a tithe.
- Financial offerings show faith that the Lord will faithfully sustain us in the future.
- Generosity expresses deep thanksgiving for the sacrifice of Christ on the cross.
